statement: The system of equations below has exactly one solution $(x, y)$. $$\begin{aligned} y &= 3x^2 - 2x - 1 \\ y &= 3x^2 + 4x + 11 \end{aligned}$$ What is the value of $y$?

choices.misconception: I found $x = -2$ correctly but computed $3(-2)^2$ as $3(-4) = -12$, so I got $-12 + 4 - 1 = -9$.
I solved for $x$ correctly and reported $x = -2$ instead of the value of $y$.
I simplified $-6x = 12$ to $x = 2$ by dropping the negative sign, and then $y = 12 - 4 - 1 = 7$.

hints: Both equations give $y$, so set their right sides equal.
The $3x^2$ terms cancel, leaving the linear equation $-2x - 1 = 4x + 11$.
Solving gives $x = -2$; substitute it into either equation to get $y$.

solutions.reliable: Setting $3x^2 - 2x - 1 = 3x^2 + 4x + 11$ and subtracting $3x^2$ from both sides gives $-2x - 1 = 4x + 11$, so $-6x = 12$ and $x = -2$. Then $y = 3(4) - 2(-2) - 1 = 12 + 4 - 1 = 15$. Check with the other equation: $3(4) + 4(-2) + 11 = 12 - 8 + 11 = 15$.
